pages.title: Relationship Workshops in Austin: How to Choose One
pages.short_answer: Austin's relationship workshops fall into three groups: method-based couples workshops (Gottman's Art and Science of Love and Imago's Getting the Love You Want), therapist-led couples retreats, and experiential programs like WeDeepen's Love Immersion, a three-day in-person retreat open to couples and solo participants. Choose a method-based workshop for a structured protocol with your partner; choose WeDeepen to practice love with several teachers, partnered or not.
pages.meta_description: Compare relationship workshops in Austin: Gottman, Imago, therapist-led retreats, and WeDeepen's Love Immersion. Who each fits and whether you need a partner.
pages.content_html:
Search "relationship workshops in Austin" and you get a mix of very different things under one label. Some are clinical programs that teach one research-backed method to couples. Some are therapist-led retreats. Some are experiential weekends where you practice connection with other people in the room. They all count as workshops, but they suit different people. This guide sorts them out so you can pick the one that fits where your love life actually is.

The main relationship workshops in Austin

Gottman: The Art and Science of Love

The Center for Relationships in Austin runs the Gottman Institute's two-day couples retreat, The Art and Science of Love, led by Dr. Vagdevi Meunier, a Gottman Master Trainer. The format mixes presentations with exercises each couple does privately. It rests on John and Julie Gottman's research into what separates relationships that last from ones that don't: friendship, managing conflict, and building shared meaning. Dates are listed on the Gottman Institute's event page.

Best for: committed couples who want a structured, research-based protocol and a shared vocabulary for conflict.

Imago: Getting the Love You Want

Imago Texas offers the Getting the Love You Want couples workshop, roughly 18 to 20 hours over two and a half days, with in-person dates in Austin and other Texas cities. It follows the Imago approach created by Dr. Harville Hendrix and Dr. Helen LaKelly Hunt, which centers on a structured dialogue that helps partners hear each other without defending.

Best for: couples stuck in the same argument who want one clear technique to practice at home.

Therapist-led couples retreats

Several Austin practices run their own intensives and retreats, for example Krista J Miller's couples workshops and retreats. These usually sit closer to therapy: a licensed clinician, a small number of couples, and a focus on a specific problem. Check the credentials and the method before you book.

Best for: couples who want clinical depth in a concentrated format.

WeDeepen Love Immersion

Love Immersion is WeDeepen's three-day, in-person retreat in Austin. It looks different from the clinical options: live "hot seat" coaching where people work on what they actually came with, connection exercises that land in the body rather than the head, and long stretches of unstructured time with the other participants. It isn't built on one method. The faculty are senior teachers from different traditions, chosen by founder Christina Weber. About half of every Love Immersion arrives solo, and participants have ranged from 18 to 87. It costs $2,995 per person, with a payment plan at checkout.

Best for: anyone, partnered or not, who wants to study love with several teachers and practice it with real people.

WeDeepen Membership (online, every week)

If a weekend feels like too big a first step, the WeDeepen Membership runs a 90-minute live session every Tuesday at 6:00 PM Central, alternating Love Masterminds with guest experts and Integration Sessions where you practice what you learned. It includes a private community and a weekly Sunday Dare. It's $99 a month, and you can cancel anytime.

How the options compare

Imago Getting the Love You WantAbout 2.5 days, couplesYesStructured dialogue
Therapist-led retreatsVaries; small groups or privateUsuallyClinical
WeDeepen Love Immersion3-day in-person retreat in AustinNo; about half come soloMultiple teachers, live coaching, practice
WeDeepen MembershipWeekly live online sessions plus communityNoOngoing practice with rotating experts

How to choose

Start with three questions.

  • Are you coming as a couple? Gottman and Imago workshops are designed for two partners working together. If you're single, dating, or your partner isn't ready, choose a format that welcomes you on your own.
  • Do you want one method or many? A single method gives you a clean toolkit. Several teachers give you range, and you keep what works for you.
  • Do you want to learn about love or practice it? Some workshops mostly teach. Others put you in live exercises with other people. Both have value; know which one you're signing up for.

Workshop or therapy?

A relationship workshop is education. It teaches skills and gives you a place to practice them. It is not a substitute for therapy. If you're dealing with abuse, addiction, or a mental-health crisis, start with a licensed clinician. Many couples do both: therapy for the hard history, a workshop for new skills and fresh air.

Where WeDeepen fits

WeDeepen starts from a simple premise: love is a trainable skill. You don't need a crisis, a breakup, or a partner to get better at it. Every WeDeepen experience runs on the Four Pillars: growth comes first, with no attachment to outcome; you own your own experience; all feelings are welcome; and the relationship is a place to practice love. Read what past participants say, check the events calendar, or join the membership and start this Tuesday. Come play with us.

FAQ

Do I need a partner to attend a relationship workshop in Austin?

For Gottman and Imago couples workshops, yes. WeDeepen's Love Immersion and Membership welcome individuals, and about half of every Love Immersion arrives solo.

How long are relationship workshops?

Most run two to three days. The Gottman Art and Science of Love is two days, Imago's Getting the Love You Want is about two and a half, and WeDeepen's Love Immersion is three full days in Austin. WeDeepen's Membership meets weekly online.

Is a relationship workshop the same as couples therapy?

No. A workshop teaches skills to a group; therapy treats a specific couple's situation with a licensed clinician. WeDeepen is relationship education and coaching, not therapy.

What happens at a WeDeepen Love Immersion?

Three days of live coaching, connection exercises, teaching from several faculty members, and unstructured time with the group, at a private venue in Austin. You can come alone, with a partner, a friend, or a family member.

Is there something smaller to try first?

Yes. The WeDeepen Membership is $99 a month for a live online session every Tuesday plus a private community, and you can cancel anytime.

pages.title: The Best Ways to Meet People in Austin
pages.short_answer: The best ways to meet people in Austin put you in the same room with the same people more than once: recreational leagues like Austin Sports & Social Club, run clubs, Meetup groups, volunteering, hosted dinners like Timeleft, and connection-focused communities like WeDeepen, which runs weekly sessions and in-person Austin events. Repetition and shared activity matter more than the venue.
pages.meta_description: The best ways to meet people in Austin: sports leagues, run clubs, Meetup, volunteering, Timeleft dinners, and WeDeepen's connection community and events.
keywords: best ways to meet people in austin
pages.content_html:
Austin is full of people who moved here recently, work from home, and still haven't found their people. The city has plenty to do. What's harder to find is the thing that actually builds connection: seeing the same faces again and again, doing something together, and having at least one real conversation. Here are the ways that work, and how to choose between them.

Why repetition beats one-off events

A single mixer rarely turns into a relationship of any kind. Research by University of Kansas professor Jeffrey Hall found it takes roughly 50 hours together to go from acquaintance to casual friend, and more than 200 hours to become close friends. So the best way to meet people isn't the most exciting event in town. It's the one you'll keep going back to.

The best ways to meet people in Austin

Recreational sports leagues

Austin Sports & Social Club runs coed adult leagues across about ten sports, including volleyball, soccer, kickball, and pickleball, with a happy hour after games. A season gives you a built-in team and a weekly reason to show up. You don't need to be good, just willing.

Run clubs

Austin's run clubs are some of the most social in the country. Austin Runners Club lists weekly training and social runs, and Austin Fit Magazine's run club roundup covers the central-city groups where the post-run hang matters as much as the miles.

Meetup groups

Meetup's Austin social groups cover everything from board games to hiking to groups made for newcomers. Choose a small group that meets often over a large one that meets rarely.

Volunteering

United Way for Greater Austin's Hands On Central Texas program has long connected Austin volunteers with local projects. Volunteering gives you a shared purpose and a natural conversation starter, and recurring shifts put you next to the same people week after week.

Dinners with strangers

Timeleft matches you with a small group for a weekly dinner at a local restaurant, based on a personality questionnaire. Time Out tried it in Austin. It's a low-pressure way to practice talking to new people.

City classes

Austin Parks and Recreation community centers offer adult classes from arts and crafts to pickleball. A class has a built-in schedule and a shared beginner's awkwardness, which helps.

Connection-focused communities: WeDeepen

Most options above build connection as a side effect of an activity. WeDeepen makes connection the point. The Austin-based relationship education company runs a weekly live online session every Tuesday at 6:00 PM Central, a private member community, in-person events in Austin, and the three-day Love Immersion retreat. The conversations go past small talk on purpose: dating, partnership, desire, conflict, and what you actually want. Members are partnered, dating, between relationships, or just curious. About half of every Love Immersion arrives solo.

How to make it stick

  • Commit to three visits. The first time is always awkward. By the third, people recognize you.
  • Pick one recurring thing, then add one. Two regular commitments beat ten one-off events.
  • Ask a real question. "What brought you to Austin?" opens more than "What do you do?"
  • Make the second plan yourself. Suggest coffee or the next event. Most people are waiting for someone else to ask.
  • Notice what you bring. If you hold back to avoid looking eager, you're shrinking. Connection rewards the person who shows up fully.

Where WeDeepen fits

WeDeepen treats connection the way a gym treats strength: love is a trainable skill, and you get better by practicing with other people. Sessions run on the Four Pillars, so all feelings are welcome and you own your own experience. WeDeepen's view is that community is your third place: not home, not work, somewhere you're known. Start with the $99 monthly membership, come to an in-person event, and see who you meet. Come play with us.

FAQ

What is the best way to meet people in Austin?

Join something that repeats, like a sports league, run club, volunteer shift, or community such as WeDeepen, and keep going back. Seeing the same people over time builds connection faster than one-off events.

Is Austin a hard city to meet people in?

It can feel that way because so many residents are newcomers or work remotely. The upside is that a lot of people are looking, so recurring groups tend to welcome new faces.

How can I meet people in Austin without drinking?

Run clubs, volunteering, city classes, morning sports, and WeDeepen's weekly online sessions all work without a bar.

Can I join WeDeepen if I'm not looking for a partner?

Yes. WeDeepen is for anyone who wants to get better at love and connection, including friendships, family, and the relationship with yourself.

Is WeDeepen therapy?

No. WeDeepen is relationship education and coaching. It is not therapy or a substitute for mental-health treatment.

pages.short_answer: To make friends in Austin as an adult, pick one or two recurring activities and keep showing up, then turn familiar faces into specific plans: a league through Austin Sports & Social Club, a run club, a Meetup group, a Timeleft dinner, or Bumble For Friends. Research suggests casual friendship takes about 50 hours together. If you want deeper conversation from the start, WeDeepen's community is built around it.

pages.content_html:
Making friends as an adult in Austin has a specific shape. Many people here are transplants, plenty work remotely, and the friends from school or your last city are a flight away. None of that means something is wrong with you. Adult friendship just doesn't happen by accident the way it did at school, so you have to build the conditions for it on purpose.

Friendship takes time, so plan for it

University of Kansas researcher Jeffrey Hall estimated the hours it takes: about 50 hours together to go from acquaintance to casual friend, about 90 to become friends, and more than 200 to become close friends. You won't get there through one happy hour. You get there by putting yourself somewhere you'll see the same people every week.

Where adults in Austin make friends

A recurring team or league

Austin Sports & Social Club runs coed adult leagues in about ten sports, with games in neighborhoods across the city and a social hour afterward. You can sign up alone and get placed on a team.

A run club

Austin Runners Club offers weekly training and social runs, and the Austin Insider running guide covers the trails and groups at the heart of the city's running scene. Runs are easy to drop into, and coffee afterward is where friendships start.

A Meetup group built for newcomers

Meetup's Austin social category includes groups made specifically for people new to the city or looking for friends. Smaller groups that meet weekly are where you'll start recognizing people.

A friendship app

Bumble For Friends works like a dating app for platonic connection. It helps you find people; turning a match into a friend still takes repeated plans in person.

A table of strangers

Timeleft books you into a weekly dinner with a small group matched by personality. One dinner won't make a friend, but it's good practice, and some tables keep meeting.

A community built around deeper conversation

If small talk is what wears you out, WeDeepen is built for the conversations most groups avoid. The Austin-based relationship education company runs a live online session every Tuesday at 6:00 PM Central, a private community, in-person events in Austin, and the three-day Love Immersion retreat. People come to get better at love in all its forms: friendship, dating, partnership, and the relationship with themselves. Plenty come on their own.

From acquaintance to friend

  • Be the one who invites. Most people want more friends and wait for someone else to make the plan. Make it.
  • Make specific plans. "Want to get tacos after Thursday's run?" works better than "We should hang out sometime."
  • Follow up within a week. Momentum matters more than polish.
  • Go a level deeper. Share something true about your week, not just the highlights. Closeness grows when both people risk a little.
  • Stop shrinking. If you mute yourself to seem easygoing, people meet a version of you that isn't real. Let them meet the real one.

Friendship is a skill

WeDeepen's premise is that love is a trainable skill, and friendship is one of its purest forms. Listening without fixing, asking for what you want, repairing after a misstep: you can practice all of these. Every WeDeepen session runs on the Four Pillars, including that you own your own experience and that all feelings are welcome. It's a room where you can practice being known, and then take that into the rest of your life. Start with the $99 monthly membership or meet people at an Austin event. Come play with us.

FAQ

How do I make friends in Austin as an adult?

Join one or two recurring activities, like a league, run club, Meetup group, or community such as WeDeepen, then turn repeat faces into specific plans. Research suggests friendship takes dozens of hours together, so consistency matters most.

Is it normal to struggle to make friends after moving to Austin?

Yes. Many Austin residents moved here as adults or work remotely, so lots of people are in the same position, which makes newcomer groups easier to join.

What are good friend-making activities in Austin for introverts?

Small recurring groups work best: a book club, a volunteer shift, a class, or WeDeepen's online Tuesday session, where you can listen first and speak when you're ready.

Can I join WeDeepen just to make friends?

Yes. You don't need to be dating or partnered. WeDeepen is for anyone who wants deeper connection, including friendship.

How much does WeDeepen cost?

The WeDeepen Membership is $99 a month or $990 a year, and you can cancel anytime. Love Immersion, the three-day retreat in Austin, is $2,995 per person.

The good news is that Austin is one of the easier cities to meet people in person, if you know where to look. Here are the main alternatives to dating apps, what each one does well, and how to choose.

Why in-person beats the feed

Apps are good at one thing: showing you a lot of people fast. They're bad at the information that actually predicts attraction and compatibility: how someone listens, how they laugh, how they treat the server, what it feels like to sit next to them. Meeting in person gives you all of that in the first five minutes. The alternatives below trade volume for that kind of signal.

Alternatives to dating apps in Austin

Speed dating events

If you like the efficiency of apps but want to meet face to face, speed dating is the closest swap. CitySwoon runs matched speed dating nights at Austin venues, and Cheeky Date hosts age-bracketed events in East Austin, South Austin, and downtown. You meet several people in one evening and match afterward.

Hosted dinners

Timeleft seats you with a small group of strangers at a weekly dinner. It's billed as a way to make friends, not dates, and that lower pressure is part of the appeal. Conversation flows better when no one is auditioning.

Social sports and run clubs

Austin Sports & Social Club leagues and Austin Runners Club group runs give you something to do together every week. Attraction builds slowly here, which is often how the best relationships start.

Interest groups

Meetup's Austin social groups cover hiking, dancing, board games, and more. You meet people who already share at least one thing you care about.

Matchmaking

Matchmakers do the filtering for you. WeDeepen's Love Club, its $9,997-a-year inner circle, includes Collaborative Matchmaking with partner matchmakers, alongside coaching and community.

Connection-focused community: WeDeepen

WeDeepen isn't a dating service. It's an Austin-based relationship education company where people practice the skills that make dating work: honest conversation, reading attraction, asking for what you want, and handling rejection without shrinking. Members meet in a live online session every Tuesday at 6:00 PM Central, in a private community, at in-person events in Austin, and at the three-day Love Immersion retreat. You meet people who are working on themselves, which makes them more interesting to meet.

How to choose

  • Want volume? Speed dating gives you the most new people per evening.
  • Want low pressure? Dinners, leagues, and interest groups let attraction show up on its own schedule.
  • Want help? Matchmaking filters for you.
  • Want to get better at dating itself? A community like WeDeepen builds the skills you take to every first date. Pair it with any of the options above.

Make any first meeting count

Whichever route you choose, the first conversation matters. Ask questions you actually want answered, share something real, and notice how you feel around the person, not just whether they check boxes. For prompts that go past small talk, see first date conversation ideas on the WeDeepen blog, and compatibility vs. chemistry for telling a spark from a fit.

The community runs on the Four Pillars: growth comes first, with no attachment to outcome; you own your own experience; all feelings are welcome; and every relationship is a place to practice love. That frame takes the pressure off any single date. If you're ready to expand your range beyond the apps, start with the $99 monthly membership. Come play with us.

If that sounds familiar, here's what to try instead, and how to get more out of speed dating if you still like it.

What speed dating does well, and where it falls short

Speed dating works because it's in person and efficient. You get the read you can't get from a profile: voice, presence, chemistry. It falls short because the format rewards quick performance over real connection. Many interesting people warm up slowly, and a short timer cuts them off before they get going. The alternatives below keep the in-person signal and give conversations more room.

If you like the format: speed dating in Austin

CitySwoon runs matched "Speed Dating 2.0" nights at Austin venues, with phone check-in and live-selected mini-dates. Cheeky Date hosts host-led, age-bracketed events in East Austin, South Austin, and downtown. Aggregators like Event Flo list other upcoming events.

Interest groups and run clubs

Meetup groups and Austin Runners Club social runs put you side by side doing something you enjoy. That takes the pressure off and lets attraction build.

Connection workshops and community: WeDeepen

WeDeepen is the opposite of an eight-minute interview. It's an Austin-based relationship education community where people practice connection on purpose, through guided exercises, honest sharing, and coaching from experienced faculty. It meets online every Tuesday at 6:00 PM Central, at in-person events in Austin, and at the three-day Love Immersion retreat. It's not a dating event, but it's a room full of open, curious people who want deeper connection, and about half of every Love Immersion arrives solo.

  • Skip the résumé questions. Ask what someone is excited about this month, not what they do for work.

Where WeDeepen fits

Speed dating tests you on the spot. WeDeepen trains the skill underneath. Love is a trainable skill, and the people who date well have practiced presence, curiosity, and asking for what they want. WeDeepen runs on the Four Pillars: growth comes first, you own your own experience, all feelings are welcome, and relationships are a place to practice love. Go to speed dating if you like it. pages.title: Dating Coach in Austin: What They Do and How to Choose
pages.short_answer: A dating coach in Austin helps you get clear on what you want, see the patterns you repeat, and practice the conversations that matter. Coaching isn't therapy and isn't matchmaking. Look for real training, such as an International Coaching Federation credential. WeDeepen founder Christina Weber, an ICF-certified coach, offers private sessions on Zoom, plus a weekly membership and Austin retreats to practice in.
pages.meta_description: What an Austin dating coach does, how coaching differs from therapy and matchmaking, which credentials matter, and how WeDeepen's coaching and community fit.
pages.content_html:
A dating coach in Austin helps you get better at the part of love you can practice: how you meet people, what you notice on a first date, how you say what you want, and why the same pattern keeps showing up. This guide covers what dating coaches actually do, how they differ from therapists and matchmakers, which credentials mean something, and how WeDeepen fits if you want coaching plus a community to practice in.

What a dating coach does

Coaching works on where you are now and where you want to go. A good dating coach helps you get clear on what you want in a partner, look honestly at the patterns you repeat, practice conversations you've been avoiding, and make decisions faster. Some coaches focus on tactics like profiles and openers. Others go deeper into attachment, self-worth, and the parts of you that show up when someone good arrives.

Christina Weber, WeDeepen's founder, works in the deeper lane. Her first question for every client is the same: how's your love life? In private sessions on Zoom, she maps how you love, decide, and connect, sometimes drawing on the Erotic Blueprints and WeDeepen's Four Pillars, and sends you off with something specific to practice. Love is a trainable skill, and coaching is the reps.

Dating coach, therapist, or matchmaker

These three get blurred, but they do different jobs:

  • A therapist is licensed to treat mental-health conditions and work through past hurt, trauma, and attachment wounds. If depression, anxiety, or trauma is driving your dating life, start there.
  • A dating coach works on you: your clarity, your habits, your choices, and the skills you bring into a room. Coaching isn't therapy and doesn't replace it.
  • A matchmaker runs the search for you, finding and vetting people outside your circle and setting up introductions. As one matchmaking firm puts it, a matchmaker is hired to run the search itself.

Many people benefit from more than one. WeDeepen's Love Club, for example, pairs coaching and education with Collaborative Matchmaking through partner matchmakers.

Credentials worth checking

Anyone can call themselves a dating coach, so ask about training. The most widely recognized coaching credentials come from the International Coaching Federation. Its three levels are:

  • ACC: 60+ hours of coach education and 100+ hours of coaching experience.
  • PCC: 125+ hours of education and 500+ hours of experience.
  • MCC: 200+ hours of education and 2,500+ hours of experience.

Christina Weber is an ICF-certified coach trained at iPEC. She has also been producing dating, relationship, and intimacy events since 2014, reaching more than 40,000 people.

Credentials aren't everything. Ask how the coach works, what a typical session looks like, and whether they'll tell you the truth when you'd rather not hear it.

Questions to ask before you hire one

  • Do you work with my situation: dating again after divorce, dating while partnered, or deciding whether to stay?
  • Will my partner be able to join sessions if we start dating seriously?
  • What will I practice between sessions?
  • How do you know when to refer me to a therapist?
  • Is there a way to keep practicing with other people, not just with you?

That last question matters more than most people expect. Coaching gives you insight. Practice with real people turns it into skill.

How WeDeepen fits

WeDeepen is an Austin relationship education company, not a dating app. You can work with it at three depths:

  • Private coaching with Christina: one-on-one or couples sessions on Zoom. A first session is $295, credited toward her Love Accelerator mentorship if you continue. Book a session.
  • The WeDeepen Membership: $99/month or $990/year, with a 90-minute live session every Tuesday at 6 PM Central and a private community. It's a place to practice love every week with people who take it seriously. Join the membership.

Coaching works best when growth comes first, with no attachment to outcome. You don't have to be in crisis, and you don't need a partner to start. Come play with us.

FAQ

Is a dating coach the same as a therapist?

No. A therapist is licensed to treat mental-health conditions and past trauma. A dating coach focuses on your present choices, skills, and patterns in dating. Coaching isn't a substitute for therapy.

Do dating coaches in Austin work in person or online?

What credential should a dating coach have?

Can couples see a dating coach?

pages.title: Intimacy Coach in Austin: What to Expect and How to Choose
pages.short_answer: An intimacy coach helps you build emotional, physical, and sexual closeness through conversation, guided exercises, and practice. It's coaching, not therapy. For sexual pain, trauma, or mental-health concerns, see a licensed sex therapist; AASECT certifies them. In Austin, WeDeepen offers private coaching with Christina Weber, a weekly online membership taught by intimacy and somatic experts, and in-person Love Immersion retreats.
pages.meta_description: What an intimacy coach does, how it differs from a sex therapist, frameworks like the Erotic Blueprints, and intimacy coaching at WeDeepen in Austin.
pages.content_html:
An intimacy coach helps individuals and couples build closeness: emotional, physical, and sexual. Sessions are mostly conversation and practice, with exercises you take home. It's education and coaching, not therapy and not hands-on bodywork. In Austin, you'll find intimacy coaches working privately, licensed sex therapists in clinical practice, and group programs like WeDeepen's workshops and retreats. This guide explains the differences so you can choose.

What an intimacy coach works on

Common reasons people come to an intimacy coach:

  • Desire has faded in a long relationship, or you and your partner want different things.
  • You struggle to say what you want, in bed or out of it.
  • You feel armored, and keep people at a distance even when you want them close.
  • You want to explore something new, like Tantra, kink, or opening a relationship, with guidance.
  • You're dating again and want to understand your own patterns first.

A lot of the work is about the nervous system. WeDeepen faculty member Kimi Inch, a somatic therapist, put it this way on Christina Weber's podcast: "If we are struggling to keep a regulated nervous system, it's really hard for us to step into our pleasure and to be in deep connection and intimacy with another." Our guide to that episode covers how safety is built step by step.

Intimacy coach vs. sex therapist

The difference is training and scope:

  • A sex therapist is a licensed mental-health clinician. The American Association of Sexuality Educators, Counselors and Therapists (AASECT) certifies sex therapists, who need at least a master's degree in a clinical field that includes psychotherapy training, plus supervised experience. See a sex therapist for sexual pain, trauma, compulsive behavior, or anything tied to a mental-health condition.
  • An intimacy coach isn't licensed to treat conditions. Coaches focus on skills, communication, and practice. Training varies widely, so ask. AASECT also certifies sexuality educators and counselors, and the International Coaching Federation credentials coaches in general.

If you're unsure, start with a consultation and ask the coach directly when they'd refer you to a therapist. A good coach will have a clear answer.

Frameworks you may hear about

Intimacy coaches often draw on a few common maps:

  • The Erotic Blueprints, created by Jaiya: five arousal types (Energetic, Sensual, Sexual, Kinky, Shapeshifter). Knowing your mix and your partner's makes it easier to meet each other.
  • Somatic and embodiment work: practices that bring attention into the body so you feel what you want, not just think it.
  • Tantra and conscious kink: structured, consent-based ways to explore energy, power, and play.
  • Attachment-focused approaches: such as Emotionally Focused Therapy, used in Hold Me Tight workshops in Austin run by therapists.

One-on-one coaching or a group

Private coaching gives you focus and privacy. Groups give you something private sessions can't: you learn by watching others work through what you're facing, and you practice with real people. At WeDeepen's Love Immersion retreats, participants take turns in live "hot seats" with two expert coaches, and everyone learns from each turn. All feelings are welcome, and you own your own experience: every exercise is an invitation, never a demand.

Many people do both. A few private sessions help you get clear on what you want to work on. A group then gives you a place to practice it, with feedback from people who aren't your partner and have no stake in being polite.

Intimacy coaching at WeDeepen

WeDeepen is an Austin relationship education company built on one idea: love is a trainable skill. Options:

  • Private coaching with Christina Weber, an ICF-certified coach trained at iPEC, one-on-one or as a couple on Zoom. A first session is $295. Book a session.
  • The WeDeepen Membership, $99/month, with a live session every Tuesday at 6 PM Central, taught by a rotating faculty of intimacy, somatic, and relationship experts. Join the membership.
  • Love Immersion, three days in person in Austin, $2,995 per person, solo or with a partner.

Meet the teachers on the faculty page. Come play with us.

FAQ

Is intimacy coaching physical?

Generally no. Most intimacy coaching is conversation, guided exercises, and practices you do on your own or with a partner. Ask any coach to explain their boundaries before you book.

Do I need a partner to see an intimacy coach?

No. Many people work on intimacy while single, so they show up differently in their next relationship.

What's the difference between an intimacy coach and a sex therapist?

A sex therapist is a licensed clinician who can treat sexual and mental-health conditions. An intimacy coach focuses on skills, communication, and practice and doesn't provide therapy.

How do I find a certified sex therapist in Austin?

AASECT, the main certifying body in the US, certifies sex therapists, sexuality counselors, and sexuality educators.

Is WeDeepen therapy?

No. WeDeepen is relationship education and coaching, not a substitute for mental-health treatment.

pages.meta_description: Compare couples retreats in Texas: Gottman, Imago, and Hold Me Tight workshops, private therapy intensives, and WeDeepen's Love Immersion near Austin.
pages.content_html:
Couples retreats in Texas come in three main formats: method-based weekend workshops (Gottman, Imago, and Hold Me Tight), private intensives with a single therapist, and experiential retreats like WeDeepen's Love Immersion in the Austin Hill Country. The right one depends on whether you want a structured method, clinical depth on one problem, or a broader place to practice love. This guide walks through each so you can pick.

Start with what you want out of it

Before comparing venues and dates, get honest about why you're going:

  • You keep having the same fight. A method-based workshop gives you one shared tool and vocabulary.
  • Something specific broke, like an affair, a loss, or a long freeze. A private intensive with a licensed therapist is usually the better fit.
  • Nothing is wrong, but you want more. More aliveness, more honesty, more play. An experiential retreat fits here.
  • Only one of you wants to go. Look for a retreat that welcomes solo participants, so the willing partner can start.

Method-based couples workshops

These follow a published approach and are taught by trained leaders, usually over a weekend.

  • Gottman, The Art and Science of Love. A two-day workshop. According to the Gottman Institute, day one covers the research and foundational skills, and day two focuses on managing conflict and communicating. It runs online and in person, including in Austin through the Center for Relationships.
  • Imago, Getting the Love You Want. Imago Texas runs this workshop, about 18 to 20 hours over two and a half days, in several Texas cities. It centers on a structured dialogue.
  • Hold Me Tight. Based on Dr. Sue Johnson's Emotionally Focused Therapy. Therapists offer it in Austin, for example A New Therapy, and elsewhere in Texas, such as Lifegrowth.

These are strong when both partners want to learn the same method. They're less suited to couples who want to explore beyond conflict, like desire, play, or who they each are becoming.

Private couples intensives

A private intensive puts one couple with one therapist for a concentrated block, from a few hours to several days. A New Therapy in Austin, for example, lists three-day Emotionally Focused Therapy intensives as well as shorter sessions. These sit closest to therapy. Choose one when the stakes are high and you want clinical care. Check the therapist's license and method before you book.

Experiential retreats

Experiential retreats are less about one method and more about practice. WeDeepen's Love Immersion is three days in person at HAVAN Estates, a private venue in the Texas Hill Country outside Austin. About 30 participants work with six coaches. The core is live hot-seat coaching: you bring what's most alive in your love life to two experts, then learn again by watching everyone else take their turn. The weekend also includes teachings, embodied practice, games, and shared meals.

Love Immersion runs on WeDeepen's Four Pillars: growth comes first, with no attachment to outcome; you own your own experience; all feelings are welcome; and the relationship is a place to practice love. It's open to couples and to people who come solo, with a friend, or with a family member. About half arrive solo. Participants rate it 9.6 out of 10, and 70% come back for another.

It's relationship education and coaching, not therapy. If you're in crisis, start with a therapist and add a retreat later.

Questions to ask any retreat

  • Who leads it, and what is their training?
  • How much time is group teaching versus private work as a couple?
  • Can one partner come alone?
  • What happens after the weekend: is there follow-up or a community?
  • What is the refund or transfer policy?

On the last point: Love Immersion tickets are $2,995 per person, with a payment plan at checkout. They're non-refundable but fully transferable.

Keep practicing after the weekend

Every retreat leader will tell you the same thing: the weekend is the start, not the finish. Love is a trainable skill, and skills fade without practice. The WeDeepen Membership gives you a 90-minute live session every Tuesday at 6 PM Central and a private community, for $99/month. Join the membership before or after your retreat. Come play with us.

FAQ

How long is a typical couples retreat in Texas?

Most run two to three days. Gottman's Art and Science of Love is two days, Imago's Getting the Love You Want is about two and a half, and Love Immersion is three.

Is a couples retreat the same as couples therapy?

Not always. Private intensives with a licensed therapist are therapy. Method workshops and experiential retreats like Love Immersion are education and practice.

Can I go to a couples retreat without my partner?

Some retreats require couples. Love Immersion welcomes solo participants, and about half arrive solo.

Where is Love Immersion held?

At HAVAN Estates, a private venue in the Hill Country at 17301 Flint Rock Rd, Austin, TX 78738. Meals are included; lodging is booked separately.

Are couples retreats in Texas held online too?

Some are. The Gottman Institute runs The Art and Science of Love as a live virtual event as well as in person.

pages.meta_description: What happens at WeDeepen's Love Immersion: three days of hot-seat coaching in Austin, who teaches and attends, the Four Pillars, cost, venue, and logistics.
pages.content_html:
A Love Immersion is WeDeepen's three-day, in-person relationship retreat in Austin, Texas. The format is a "love mastermind": about 30 participants and six coaches, built around live hot-seat coaching, plus teachings, embodied practice, play, and shared meals. You can come solo or with a partner. This page covers what happens over the three days, who goes, what it costs, and how it differs from a workshop or therapy.

Where the name comes from

Most of us reach adulthood with years of education and almost none in love. We follow chemistry, learn through heartbreak, and hope experience eventually turns into wisdom. Christina Weber, who founded WeDeepen, designed Love Immersion to make that learning intentional. The idea is total immersion, the way you'd learn a language: three days in which love is the only subject. The tagline for the current edition is "Mastermind your love life."

What happens over three days

The center of the weekend is the Masterminding Love hot seat. You bring what's most alive in your love life, whether that's a decision, a pattern, a conversation you're dreading, or a desire you haven't named, to two expert coaches. They help you see what's really happening and how to move forward. Then you learn again by watching everyone else take their turn. Other people's questions, blind spots, and courage often show you things you couldn't see in your own life.

Around the hot seats, the weekend includes:

  • Workshops and interactive exercises for clearer, more connected relationships.
  • Play and connection: Truth or Dare, games, and surprises.
  • Shared meals, all included.
  • Integration and a graduation ceremony on the last day, with community support after.

The October 2026 edition, Love Immersion VIII, runs Saturday through Monday. The first day starts at 9 AM with breakfast and an opening circle, and the retreat closes around 2 PM on the third day. The full schedule is on the Love Immersion VIII page.

Who teaches it

There's no single guru or method. The faculty are senior coaches Christina chose because they're the people she calls for guidance in her own love life. Love Immersion VIII is led by Christina Weber with Annie Lalla, Ariana Hall, Yossef Sagi, Jordan Bowditch, Rachel Cuthbert, Yarixa Ferrao, and Scott Wild. Each brings a different lens, from relationship dynamics and polarity to nervous-system healing and the one hard conversation a relationship needs. Full bios are on the faculty page.

Who goes

  • People who are dating, partnered, between relationships, or deciding whether to stay.
  • About half arrive solo. Others come with a partner, a friend, a sibling, or a parent.
  • Ages have ranged from 18 to 87, mostly people in their thirties through sixties.
  • Relationship coaches often attend as participants.

You don't need a partner, a breakup, or a crisis to come. Participants rate it 9.6 out of 10, and 70% come back. One participant, Eva Mullen, said it this way: "I didn't think I belonged. But within a day, I felt flooded with love. I felt home." More accounts are on the reviews page.

The rules of the room

Every Love Immersion runs on WeDeepen's Four Pillars: growth comes first, with no attachment to outcome; you own your own experience; all feelings are welcome, and no inner process is condemned; and the relationship is a place to practice love. In practice, that means you choose how far to go in any exercise, and nothing you feel is off-limits to bring.

Cost, venue, and logistics

  • Price: $2,995 per person, with a payment plan at checkout.
  • Refunds: tickets are non-refundable but fully transferable.
  • Venue: HAVAN Estates, a private space in the Texas Hill Country at 17301 Flint Rock Rd, Austin, TX 78738.
  • Meals: included. Lodging is booked separately, with some onsite options.
  • Travel: fly into Austin-Bergstrom (AUS).

Love Club members, at $9,997/year, get one Love Immersion credit, transferable to a partner.

Between retreats

Three days can shift a lot, and love is a trainable skill, so the practice continues. The WeDeepen Membership, $99/month or $990/year, gives you a live session every Tuesday at 6 PM Central with the same faculty, and a private community. Join the membership. Come play with us.

FAQ

Is Love Immersion therapy?

No. It's relationship education and coaching, not therapy or a substitute for mental-health treatment.

Do I need to bring a partner?

No. About half of participants come solo.

How many people attend?

About 30 participants, with six coaches, for Love Immersion VIII.

When is the next Love Immersion?

Love Immersion VIII is October 17 to 19, 2026, in Austin. Future dates are listed on the events page.

How is it different from a Gottman or Imago workshop?

Those teach one research-based method to couples. Love Immersion uses several coaches and live hot-seat work, and welcomes solo participants.
